idiom_name: typed DeadLetter<T> envelope over the transport's dead-letter mechanism (kafkajs DLT / amqplib DLX)
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds no runtime primitive, so the mechanism belongs to the transport - amqplib queue arguments with x-dead-letter-exchange, or a kafkajs producer publishing the failed record to <topic>.DLT - and TypeScript's contribution is the part that pays off in production: a single DeadLetter<T> envelope type carrying the failure metadata (original destination, reason, attempt count, timestamp, cause and the payload) so that producers, DLQ consumers and replay tooling cannot drift apart, and runtime schema validation (zod, io-ts, TypeBox) on both edges. That matters because dead-letter records are exactly the ones produced by a code path nobody exercised in happy-path tests; a typed boundary turns replay from an improvisation into a checked operation. For job queues (BullMQ) the same envelope types the failed job's data and its failedReason.
pitfalls: JSON.parse of the raw body throws for exactly the malformed payload that needs parking: parse inside its own try and fall back to a base64 body plus the parse error.
Type annotations disappear at runtime, so a DeadLetter<T> cast over unvalidated JSON lets replay tooling trust fields that were never written - validate at both produce and replay edges.
kafkajs commits offsets by topic/partition/offset string and the values are BigInt-backed: committing inside the catch before producer.send resolves loses the record when the broker is unavailable.
@types/amqplib types the arguments field loosely, so a typo in 'x-dead-letter-exchange' still compiles and produces a DLQ that never fills.
